chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad, from al-Ḥusayn, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
"If a man commits zina with a woman of unmarriageable kin, he is given the hadd of the fornicator, except that it is a greater sin."

So this does not conflict with the reports we mentioned earlier stating that a strike with the sword is obligatory upon him, because when the purpose of the strike is to kill him, and in cases where rajm is obligatory upon the fornicator and it results in death, the Imam has the choice between striking him once with the sword or stoning him.

key_terms.الْإِمَامُ مُخَيَّرٌ: the Imam is granted discretion between legal options
key_terms.حُدَّ: he is subjected to the prescribed hadd punishment
key_terms.ذَاتِ مَحْرَمٍ: a woman who is an unmarriageable kin relative
key_terms.ضَرْبَةٌ بِالسَّيْفِ: a strike with the sword as a mode of execution

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for zina with a mahram relative in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report addresses the legal ruling for zina with a mahram relative, stating that the offender receives the hadd of zina while emphasizing that the sin is graver. The accompanying explanation reconciles this with other reports by stating that where the punishment leads to death, the Imam may choose between execution by the sword and rajm.
